The shared-tier bringup runbook now scopes the analytics_reader role's workspace_records grant column-by-column, excluding provider_kind (which embeds the account email via the imbue_cloud_<email-slug> provider-instance naming) and encrypted_secrets, keeping emails out of analyst reach per the analytics identity model.

The runbook also gains a one-time production backfill section: a static signup-dimension table loaded from SuperTokens pagination (the connector-side sources undercount pre-2026-08-17 accounts), and an optional archive of the pre-0.4.2 unstructured log parquet before OpenObserve's 90-day retention discards it.

The analytics DuckDB session now sets pg_use_ctid_scan = false after every Postgres attach: the column-scoped workspace_records grant blocks reads of the ctid system column (Postgres requires table-level SELECT for system columns), which DuckDB's postgres scanner otherwise uses to parallelize scans -- without this, the staging/production aggregation fails with "permission denied for table workspace_records" even though it reads only granted columns. Found on the first staging aggregation run.

The collection poll's SSH pool is now torn down without waiting, and the whole SSH phase shares one deadline (per-workspace timeout + 120s slack) instead of granting each future its own full backstop. On the production fleet, hops to half-dead workspace sshds hang paramiko threads past every timeout; shutdown(wait=True) plus per-future backstops let those eat the entire 850s Modal budget, so every collection_poll tick was killed before recording its job_runs row (pipeline_health stayed blind to the poll) even though per-workspace collection succeeded. Found on the first hours of production collection.
